newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico recalls controversial Costa Rica envoy.
newsitem.headline: Mexico recalls controversial Costa Rica envoy.

text.p: Mexico has recalled its ambassador to Costa Rica following a furore over his comments that the Central American nation was ruled by an "oligarchy," officials said on Monday.
"(Ambassador Jose Rafael Castelazo) has been recalled for consultations," an official at the foreign ministry told Reuters.
Castelazo caused a stir in Costa Rica with a series of critical comments published in the Mexican weekly magazine Siempre about the Costa Rican political and economic system.

Costa Rica said late on Sunday that Castelazo would be transferred to another diplomatic post because of the comments. The Mexican foreign ministry official said no official decision had yet been taken.
"(Castelazo) will meet with Foreign Minister Jose Angel Gurria later this week and a decision will be taken," said the official, who requested anonymity.
Costa Rican Foreign Minister Fernando Naranjo told Reuters on Monday that the situation had been resolved after he and Gurria talked by telephone over the weekend.
"This unfortunate incident is now history, and of course it will not affect the very good relations between the two countries," Naranjo said in a telephone interview.
The remarks by Castelazo, who had just taken the post on May 22, angered Costa Ricans, who see their Central American country as relatively advanced and sophisticated.
"Even though there are two strong parties (in Costa Rica), it's the same oligarchy," Castelazo said referring to the ruling National Liberation Party and the opposition Social Christian Unit.
He also said the government of President Jose Maria Figueres "is practically paralysed because it can't make a decision."
Costa Rica demanded a retraction, but Castelazo offered neither a retraction nor an apology. He instead issued a statement praising the Costa Rican people and government.
